note:
A provider failure and then an answer. The spike met this live — Gemini returned an upstream 429 mid-run — and it is neither of ADR 0006 §2's two kinds: it is retried inside `ai` at the one place the provider is called, and the model is never told it happened.

Hand-written from the shape of `one-answer.json`, which is a real recorded exchange (M3 PR 5). Nothing here was recorded: recording a turn costs a paid call to OpenRouter, and CLAUDE.md #7 says nothing calls a paid service without the user's confirmation, which this pull request did not have. Every field but `choices` and `usage.prompt_tokens` is copied from the recorded response, so what the SDK parses is the shape a provider really sends: `provider`, `native_finish_reason`, `service_tier`, `moderation` and the rest. `usage.prompt_tokens` is set generously on purpose — the loop refuses a response whose token count says the provider dropped the prompt (ADR 0022 §3), and a hand-written 68 would have tripped it. The live run behind OPENROUTER_API_KEY is what replaces a hand-written transcript with a recorded one.
